speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Education how has the National Institute of Education been preparing trainee teachers to meet the changing demands of education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: NIE's pre-service curriculum focuses on training teachers to build character in students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Teachers learn to create lessons that harness technology, like augmented reality and virtual reality to enrich learning and help students explore beyond the confines of the physical classroom.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Teachers also learn how to make use of online tutorials, websites, artificial intelligence (AI) and chatbots to make learning more accessible to the diverse students anytime, anywhere, including those with special educational needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Additionally, teachers would also learn how technology, such as learning analytics, can be used to support students to learn in teams, and to provide choices and customised feedback for students to become self-directed in learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Last, but not least, to develop perspectives related to the community, society and the world, and to partner stakeholders like parents and the community, and industry leaders through courses, service learning, talks and seminars.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For the four-year degree programme, the pre-service teachers also have the opportunities to go for industry internship and international practicum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: NIE reviews the effectiveness of its programmes regularly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It gathers feedback from the pre-service teachers' portfolios, internal and external assessments and metric surveys.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Annual survey feedback from beginning teachers and school leaders also enables NIE to refine its pre-service programme to ensure their relevance.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond pre-service training, teachers continue deepening their competencies throughout their careers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is done through a range of in-service learning opportunities organised by MOE, NIE and the schools, including our Teacher Work Attachment Plus (TWA+) programme.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have no doubt that MOE and NIE are doing their very best.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I ask this question because we all know that the future of education, the future of work, now require very different competencies of the educators – now and in the future.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On top of what the Minister has just mentioned – and he gave a hint of all the things that they have to do – educators now take on the role of content curators and even developers, and they have to design learning experiences, they have to deliver on different platforms.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And on top of that, are expected to even be life coaches for their students.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I just wonder what kind of manpower and resources – how does NIE do it?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And are they given sufficient resources like money, manpower and even in terms of mindset, to do so, to meet these demands of the future?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, the skillsets for both the learners and the teachers will have to evolve to meet the demands of the future.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As I always share with my colleagues in MOE, teaching today is not just about the transmission of knowledge and learning is not just about the absorption of knowledge.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: A few things have changed and will continue to change.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having knowledge alone is not sufficient; what is more important is the ability to make use of the knowledge to discern and to make clear decisions, good decisions, based on sound values.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And, to this end, that is why the skillsets of our teachers must continue to evolve.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Beyond just being a transmitter of knowledge, it is increasingly important for our teachers to be able to be a facilitator in the learning environment that our students are in, for our teachers to help our students make sense of the amount of information that they come across.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: While these two things do not change, three things will need to change and evolve.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These include families, the community and also the industry.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Such technologies include the adaptive learning technologies that allow us to stretch the abilities of the high performing students while allowing us to dedicate more time to the high-needs students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, these are the new skillsets that we will require our teachers to constantly evolve.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But having said that, we do not believe that we will be able to frontload all these new skillsets even or only when they are at NIE.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: What we need is a continuous professional development programme that allows our teachers to keep learning throughout life so that they can also inspire their students to do so.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, I will pick up on the last point that Ms Denise Phua talked about.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, today, we are focused not just on the quantity – the number of teachers that we have.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: More importantly is the quality of teachers that we must have, enabled and supported by technology.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we will continue to put in efforts on this front to make sure that, given the finite number of teachers that we can have in our education system, how do we make sure that they are of the highest quality, supported by the best technology in order to stretch the abilities of our high performing students to their fullest while devoting more time to the high needs students and their families.
